basics.name: Anand Bhaskaran
basics.label: Software Engineer | Embedded Systems MSc × 2 | C++ / Python / Java | Real-Time & Large-Scale Data | Trading Interest
basics.summary: Systems engineer with dual Embedded Systems MSc (KTH, TU/e) and 3+ years of production C++ on Linux at EPFL (Robogen). Built real-time flight-control APIs as founding engineer at Dronistics and large-scale distributed data systems at Beekeeper (Kafka, ClickHouse, Elastic Search, PostgreSQL for 10M+ users). Current Lead AI Engineer at LumApps, where I ship production ML systems on GCP with cost and latency tracing. Trading domain interest: mentored Opt Alpha at Tenity on scaling high-frequency algorithmic trading in production, and run PulseView (my own real-time market intelligence product with live users). Zurich-based; Zug commutable.

work.name: LumApps
highlights: Own a production multi-agent ML system on Python + GCP Vertex AI: instrumentation for latency, cost per request, and throughput. Report to C-level on outcomes; on-call for global production.

Designed AI Brain, a temporal knowledge graph on Graphiti/Neo4j unifying 5+ data sources into one time-aware store. Event-driven ingest over Pub/Sub, concurrent read/write patterns, and freshness tracking.

work.name: Beekeeper AG
highlights: Large-scale distributed data systems for 10M+ users: Kafka event streams, ClickHouse analytics, Elastic Search indexing, PostgreSQL, K8s on AWS. Performance tuning across the stack.
Ran observability and global on-call across production systems (Grafana, Datadog, Logz.io). Debugged and optimized system behavior end to end.
Read, debugged, and improved codebases in Java, TypeScript, Python, and Vue across 3 teams. Comfortable diving into unfamiliar code and closing decisions.

work.name: Tenity
highlights: Mentored Opt Alpha on scaling high-frequency algorithmic trading systems in production. Direct exposure to HFT architecture, latency budgets, and exchange connectivity concerns.
Evaluated 20+ startups on architecture, scalability, and system design for seed-to-VC investment decisions.

work.name: Dronistics (EPFL spin-off)
highlights: Engineered real-time flight-control APIs and logistics optimization algorithms. 500+ autonomous deliveries, 99.5% safety record, zero incidents.
Built full-stack (Vue, Java, PostgreSQL) and cloud infra (AWS, Docker, Terraform) from empty repo. Deep exposure to real-time constraints and system reliability.

work.name: EPFL, Laboratory of Intelligent Systems (Robogen)
highlights: 3+ years shipping C++ in a Linux/Unix environment. Engineered Robogen, an open-source platform for co-evolution of robot bodies and neural controllers via genetic algorithms.
Migrated the simulation pipeline to AWS for large-scale parallel evolution runs. Grid-computing-style workloads across EC2; secured AWS Cloud Credits for Research.
Foundational CS work: algorithms, memory models, concurrency, neural networks, statistics, and large-scale data. Featured on the AWS Public Sector Blog.

_jobApplication.notes: STRETCH FIT. Candidate is Python/TypeScript/AI-primary, not C++ HFT-primary. Real gaps: no recent C++, no production HFT experience. Strengths reframed: Embedded Systems MSc x2 (KTH + TU/e = perfect CS foundations); 3+ yrs C++/Linux at EPFL Robogen (2016-2020); real-time systems at Dronistics; large-scale data at Beekeeper (Kafka/ClickHouse/ES/PG for 10M+ users); ML/stats big-plus is a direct hit; PulseView + Opt Alpha advisory (Tenity) = trading domain interest. Reordered education to lead with Embedded Systems MSc. Reduced LumApps to 2 bullets (AI angle less relevant), promoted EPFL to 3 (C++ signal). Zurich-based, Zug commutable. Advise a cover letter that names the gap head-on ('I am not a full-time C++ engineer today, but here is my CS foundation + my active trading-domain work').
